calibration.full_budget_plain_hill_climb_60s_x2_call: fails on both cost and determinism -- its wall-clock-time-based iteration count varies between the two required match() calls
calibration.reference_design: fixed iteration count (8000 per annealing run) x fixed restart count (15) per customer, NOT wall-clock-time-based -- confirmed byte-for-byte identical output across two consecutive match() calls with the same inputs, and confirmed to complete in ~7.6-7.8s on ordinary hardware
calibration.note: Two prior calibrations of this task were each shown wrong by direct measurement and both are reflected here. First: per-customer instances were sized (20-30 payments, 15-22 invoices; 10 customers per scenario) so that exact/brute-force solving is impractical (a bitmask DP solver was measured taking 17s at 15 payments and not finishing in 120s at 18). Second: an earlier reference used a wall-clock time budget with an adaptively-calibrated cooling schedule; a real reviewer measured that this made the reference's OWN output non-deterministic (different costs across repeated runs on a loaded host, ranging 1.02M-1.17M) and unreliable on slower hardware (a ~4x-slower-equivalent budget sometimes failed to clear the previous bar) -- directly violating the instruction's own stated determinism requirement, which also had no test coverage. Both are fixed now: the reference uses a FIXED iteration count and restart count (no wall-clock dependency at all), confirmed deterministic by direct repeated testing, and the verifier now calls match() twice per grading run specifically to test the instruction's determinism requirement (test_deterministic_output in test_scoring.py), independently of the cost-bar test. The pass bar (1,250,000 cents, ~4.9% of total value) sits just above the fixed-iteration reference's measured cost (1,150,937 cents) and far below every adversarial probe's cost, including a plain hill-climb given a full, generous wall-clock budget (which now also fails the determinism test, since its iteration count is not fixed across the two required calls).
